posts.body_html:
Naturenuts-wow, that looks great! It basically means you got one of the best original clones, haha! Honestly, I have no clue to what it exactly means. That particular clone originally came from Art Junier, and he was a computer/math nerd. Seriously, there was more to the tag than that: it said something like "XP00014560." Maybe that's the Expiration date for the plant?!

I can't see how this additional numerical code has any value to the plant, so I don't include it. Since Art is not likely on this earth anymore (we think he might have passed away), there isn't anyone who can decode it, so I only kept his original clonal information. Long story short, CH05Y means it came from Art Junier, and that's the clonal name for that unique individual.

posts.body_html: meizzwang, that's some very interesting information. I thought it was some kind of strange genetic code that I never heard of, but it turns out that it's some strange code that nobody besides Art will ever know. All I know is,  S x XP00014560 is a beautiful clone and I'm happy to have it in my collection. I may cross it with my SxWTF6969 clone next year to see what I get.

posts.body_html: Clone B in bloom 3/14. This guy bloomed on 3/27 last year, which might be more typical - its a very early spring this year here in CA. Also, the pitchers opened well after the flowers in 2014, but as you can see they are simultaneous this year. Like the rest of its black veins siblings, this plant is a dwarf - these traps are about 12" tall. Last year some of its later pitchers were closer to 16", but still...
